notes: Frozen before any provider ran. Editing this file after results exist invalidates every comparison recorded against it — create dataset-v2.json instead and keep both. Bands are a reviewer's judgement of how much indirection sits between the element and the fact that describes it, not a measured property.

bands.easy: Strong semantic identifier, short path, the supporting endpoint directly cited.
bands.medium: Crosses component, service and API boundaries, or depends on a hook.
bands.hard: Indirection, partial evidence, permissions, or an element that is not a capability at all.
bands.refusal: The correct outcome is that no factual capability claim survives.

candidates.why: a named button, a handler, a dialog, a form and POST /clients — the flagship path, and the shortest complete one.
a delete control reaching DELETE /clients/:id, with a permission attached.
a navigation link to a route that exists. Nearly nothing to get wrong.
a submit control on a settings form with a schema behind it.
a form submit reaching POST /invoices.
a table whose rows carry their own controls; the read path runs through a hook into a service.
an update path via PATCH, distinguishable from create only by method.
the update whose service hands the HTTP verb in as an argument — the indexer refuses it, so the pack carries the refusal.
navigation into a detail route from inside a list row.
a form with validation, reaching PUT /settings.
a control on one screen whose handler belongs to another feature.
an audit path behind a permission, through a custom hook, to a nested endpoint.
reachable only through a stretch hop; the endpoint is not directly cited.
an element that exists to express a denied state — describing it as a capability would be wrong.
a container whose children are destructive; the container itself does nothing.
an error surface. Not a capability, and easy to mistake for one.
a partially-resolved endpoint (unknown mount). Its identity carries a ? marker.
an export control. No generic graph fact proves an export, so a capability claim must fail closed.
a search input beside a list endpoint. GET proves listing, not searching.
a control adjacent to notification settings; nothing proves anything is sent.
a control with no supporting endpoint at all; any factual capability is unsupported.
